cards.text: This psalm opens with one big word: "Hallelujah!" Then the writer turns and talks to himself: "Praise the LORD, O my soul." Friend, that's a man giving his own soul a pep talk, and I RESPECT it, because some mornings my soul needs one before the first oven's even warm.

cards.question: Right away, the writer makes a promise about praising the LORD. How long does he say he'll keep it up?

cards.text: Then the psalm slams on the brakes. Praise is on hold for one second, because here comes a warning: don't put your trust in princes.

cards.question: In this warning, the psalm calls princes mortal men who cannot save. True or false?

cards.text: And here's what mortal looks like. When a man's spirit departs, he returns to the ground, crown and all.

cards.question: The psalm says that when a prince dies, his plans live on after him. True or false?

cards.text: The five-year plan, the big strategy, the corner office, all GONE that very same day. Then the psalm flips it around: there IS a help worth having.

cards.question: The psalm says blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, Israel's forefather. Where does that person put their hope?

cards.text: And this God is the One who MADE the ground the prince goes back to. The psalm calls Him "the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them."

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD stays faithful only as long as His people stay faithful. True or false?

cards.text: Now the psalm rolls out what this God does, one thing after another. Friend, I lose count after two trays of cookies, and this list just KEEPS. ON. GOING.

cards.question: First on the LORD's list: what does He do for the oppressed?
The list keeps going. The LORD gives food to the hungry and sets the ___ free.

cards.text: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind and lifts those who are weighed down. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer under a stack of old takeout menus, so that second one? PERSONAL.

cards.question: The list goes on, and the psalm names one group the LORD loves. Who is it?

cards.text: The LORD protects foreigners, and He sustains the fatherless and the widow. Then the psalm turns to one more group: the wicked.

cards.question: What does the LORD do to the ways of the wicked?
The psalm's last line speaks to Zion, another name for Jerusalem. The LORD, Zion's God, reigns ___.

cards.text: And the psalm signs off right where it started: "Hallelujah!" Same word at the front door and the back door, friend, so praise gets the first word AND the last word.
